correctness.rationale: Multiplying the two stages with J²=−I gives coefficients a=1−x²/2 and b=x(1+3e^(−2x²/9))/4, x=hω. The norm and determinant factor a²+b² is exactly Q(x²), strictly positive since b>0 for x>0. Planar symplecticity is equivalent to determinant one, and testing pairs of vectors supported in each canonical block makes this condition blockwise. H starts at zero with negative slope, H''>0, and H' tends to 4, giving exactly one positive crossing. Before the zero of H', H+sH'<0; after it the derivative 2H'+sH'' is strictly positive, and H+sH'>0 at the H-crossing. This proves the unique strongest damping in the stable interval. The exceptional rotation has cos θ=1−s*/2 and b>0; the certified s*<2 and cos √s*>1−s*/2 give the stated phase inequality. The Taylor expansion gives log Q(ω²h²)=−ω⁴h⁴/12+O(h⁶); multiplication by the step count gives the stated exponential limit. It also shows loss vanishes on shorter time scales and tends to full damping on longer scales at fixed ω and nonzero initial energy. Independent exact-fraction exponential enclosures reproduce the stated brackets: at the lower and upper endpoints respectively the H upper/lower bounds are about −8.524×10^−13 and +1.301×10^−12, and those of H+sH' about −1.810×10^−12 and +2.603×10^−12. The signs are certified by alternating rational sums, not the displayed rounding.
residual_risks: Exact shape values, fixed steps, positive fixed frequencies, harmonic canonical blocks, and exact arithmetic only. Strict loss or gain concerns nonzero energy; the zero mode stays zero.

originality.rationale: Gu–Chen–Jung already give the full scalar stability function; evaluating it on the imaginary axis yields the very same modal matrix and energy multiplier, so those formulas are not independent contributions. The distinct part supported here is the exact harmonic-axis classification, particularly the proof of a single positive unit-modulus crossing and a single global minimum, together with the explicit consequences and long-time coefficient. The inspected source presents a stability plot and qualitative energy behavior rather than a stronger theorem giving those classifications.
residual_risks: Best-of-knowledge statement only; no literature-wide priority certification. A related 2008 primary full text was unavailable, and the known stability formula and qualitative plot are substantial prior coverage of the analytical starting point.

value.rationale: The exact imaginary-axis crossing is the positive stability cutoff for harmonic use of a published integrator. Showing it is isolated and frequency-specific distinguishes accidental energy preservation from a structural symplectic method; locating the unique maximal-loss step and quantifying when a seemingly small decay becomes order one are useful for interpreting long runs. The contribution is the global analytical classification and its numerical meaning, not recopying the stability function or expanding a series alone.
residual_risks: This does not construct a new integrator or settle preservation on nonlinear or coupled Hamiltonian systems.
